name: Root Network
description: Subterranean neural-like system optimizing nutrient exchange and interspecies communication through soil architecture.

core_attributes.pattern: distributed allocation, soil optimization, feedback integration

scope.definition: Hydraulic efficiency of root architecture — fraction of available soil water extracted per unit root length per day at field capacity, relative to theoretical maximum given soil hydraulic conductivity.

evidence.source: Doussan et al. (1998) 'Modelling of the hydraulic architecture of root systems', Plant and Soil 206:75-88; Lynch (1995) 'Root architecture and plant productivity', Plant Physiology 109:7-13.
cross_domain_examples: maize root architecture: 0.89-0.95 of plant available water extracted during vegetative growth phase
root hair zone extends effective root radius 5-10× — increases soil volume per root length dramatically
mycorrhizal hyphae: extend effective uptake radius beyond root hair limit — 100× more soil volume accessible

scope.falsifiability: If root systems with equivalent total length but random branching architecture show identical water uptake rates to optimized architectures, geometric branching pattern provides no hydraulic advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: Efficiency drops to 0.50-0.70 as soil water potential falls below -0.3 MPa (field capacity) — soil conductivity becomes limiting. Root architecture efficiency is species-specific and deeply linked to soil type.
